person: Ruth Albers is 63 and has kept the books for the family farm in central Iowa for forty years. She and her husband Dale farm about a thousand acres of corn and soybeans, and their son Tyler is taking over the field work. An early freeze hit two nights ago, and she remembers a neighbor who lost his hail claim by missing the notice deadline. She does this on her phone at night, wants dates and field names first, and wants to know whether anything is actually filed for her or only prepared.
stated_up_front: We had that hard freeze Tuesday night and I need to know which fields need a notice in before the 72 hours is up. Don't send anything yet, just tell me which field and which date and I'll know if it's right.

portals.mine: FarmBooks notebook the son keeps on his phone

facts.truth: Low of 27 degrees on the station the night of Tuesday October 20, from about 1 to 6 a.m.

facts.about: when the freeze damage was found
facts.truth: Tyler walked the late-planted corn at the Hoffman place on Wednesday October 21 in the morning and found frozen tops and chaffy ears.
The Home 80 and the North 160 beans were cut October 12 to 14 and made 58 bushels, so nothing to notice there.
Hoffman 120 acres of corn planted June 2, still at dent and not black-layered when it froze. Guarantee is 165 bu/acre.

facts.about: rented acres not on the report
facts.truth: 30 acres rented from the Vogel estate this spring were added after the acreage report was filed. They froze too but are not on the policy.
The east 40 corn has dicamba burn, and the neighbor Gene Pruitt told Dale in a text he sprayed on a windy day in July.
The River 90 corn leaned over in the September wind but shelled out at 201 bu/acre against a guarantee of 170.
Her agent is Marlene at the Fieldmark office, who emailed in the spring confirming the acreage report.
The Schultz 100 beans were hailed in July, notice given July 9, and harvested in October. That notice is already on file.
Ruth signs for the farm. Dale and Tyler have to hear about it before anything goes to the company.

unknowns: Whether the late corn at the Hoffman place counts as freeze damage if it was already near maturity
How many days the policy gives to file the claim after harvest
Whether the Vogel acres could still be added to the policy
What price per bushel the policy uses for the indemnity
